The '''2016–17 [[La Liga]]''' season, also known as '''LaLiga [[Banco Santander|Santander]]''' for sponsorship reasons,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/laliga-and-santander-strike-title-sponsorship-deal|publisher=La Liga|date=21 July 2016|access-date=21 July 2016|title=LaLiga and Santander strike title sponsorship deal|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160725161336/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/laliga-and-santander-strike-title-sponsorship-deal|archive-date=25 July 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> was the 86th since its establishment. The season began on 19 August 2016 and concluded on 21 May 2017.

[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] secured the title following their away victory at [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] on the final matchday, finishing with 93 points and winning a record-extending 33rd championship, their first since the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/la-liga-table/2016|title=La Liga - 2016/17 Season Table|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref> [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] finished second, three points behind Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/real-madrid-crowned-201617-laliga-santander-champions|title=Real Madrid crowned 2016/17 LaLiga Santander champions|publisher=La Liga|date=21 May 2017|access-date=21 May 2017|archive-date=28 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221228150725/https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/real-madrid-crowned-201617-laliga-santander-champions|url-status=dead}}</ref> Real became only the second side after Barcelona in [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13]] to score in all 38 games of a La Liga season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2017/05/21/5921e215e5fdea41798b4607.html|title=Record breaking Real Madrid score in every game of LaLiga campaign|publisher=Marca|date=21 May 2017|access-date=21 May 2017}}</ref>

==Name sponsorship==
The Spanish top flight dropped the sponsorship from [[BBVA]] and was now called LaLiga, while the [[Segunda División|second division]] was called LaLiga2.<ref>{{cite web|title=BBVA Ends La Liga Name Sponsorship|url=http://www.footyheadlines.com/2015/09/bbva-ends-la-liga-name-sponsorship.html|publisher=Footy Headlines |access-date=4 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/javier-tebas-fans-are-always-a-priority-for-laliga|title=Javier Tebas: "Fans are always a priority for LaLiga"|publisher=LaLiga.es|date=30 June 2016|access-date=25 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160823003552/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/javier-tebas-fans-are-always-a-priority-for-laliga|archive-date=23 August 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The league made this change to maximize the La Liga brand. On 20 July, [[Banco Santander]] was appointed as the new sponsor.

===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of 20 teams contested the league, including 17 sides from the [[2015–16 La Liga|2015–16 season]] and three promoted from the [[2015–16 Segunda División]]. This included the two top teams from the Segunda División, and the winners of the [[2016 Segunda División play-offs|play-offs]].

[[Deportivo Alavés]] was the first team from Segunda División to achieve promotion, after a ten-year absence from La Liga, on 29 May 2016 after winning 2–0 against [[CD Numancia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/d-alaves-seal-promotion-whilst-leganes-and-nastic-both-win|title=D. Alaves seal promotion whilst Leganes and Nastic both win|publisher=La Liga|date=29 May 2016|access-date=30 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161010191716/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/d-alaves-seal-promotion-whilst-leganes-and-nastic-both-win|archive-date=10 October 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[CD Leganés]] was promoted as the runners-up after winning 1–0 at [[CD Mirandés]] in the last match-day, on 4 June 2016. This was Leganés' first promotion to the top division.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/leganes-make-history-by-clinching-promotion|title=Leganes win historic first promotion to Liga BBVA.|publisher=LaLiga.es|date=4 June 2016|access-date=22 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820231658/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/leganes-make-history-by-clinching-promotion|archive-date=20 August 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[CA Osasuna]] was the last to be promoted after beating [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona]] and [[Girona FC]] in the [[2016 Segunda División play-offs|play-offs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/osasuna-triumphant-in-girona-to-clinch-promotion|date=18 June 2016|title=Osasuna triumphant in Girona to clinch promotion|publisher=LaLiga.es|access-date=18 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170120183954/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/osasuna-triumphant-in-girona-to-clinch-promotion|archive-date=20 January 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Reds returned to La Liga two years after their last relegation.

The three promoted clubs replaced [[Rayo Vallecano]], [[Getafe CF|Getafe]], and [[Levante UD|Levante]], who were relegated at the end of the previous season after five, twelve, and six years respectively.

===Zamora Trophy===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy]] was awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest ratio of goals conceded to matches played. A goalkeeper had to play at least 28 matches of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/trofeos/2015-2016/zamora/primera.html|title=Trofeo Zamora La Liga Santander|newspaper=Marca|language=es}}</ref>
